audit_metadata.phase: Phase 7.1 Sowing Trigger, Agricultural Evidence and Scientific Consistency Audit

rain_shadow_anomaly_diagnosis.anomaly_statement: Rain Shadow reached 50 mm trigger at DOY 166.1 (June 15) vs Core Interior at DOY 168.4 (June 17-18) despite receiving 36% less June rainfall.
primary_causes: Survivor/Selection Bias: In Phase 7, np.nanmedian dropped cell-years failing to reach 50 mm. In Rain Shadow, 10.04% of years never reached 50 mm by July 15 and 14.39% were delayed into July. Dropping unreached years artificially accelerated the apparent median.

Episodic Pre-Monsoon Convective Storms: In Rain Shadow, the single wettest day accounts for 57.3% of the 50 mm trigger (mean max 1-day rain = 28.66 mm over just 2.6 rainy days), delivering rain in intense, isolated bursts rather than synoptic monsoon progression.

High Post-Trigger Break Risk: Within 20 days post-trigger, Rain Shadow suffers a >= 10-day severe dry spell in 39.13% of triggered years (and >= 7-day break in 61.22% of years), compared to only 12.56% and 34.02% in Core Interior.

Rolling Window Reachability Failure: When tested on rolling 3-day and 5-day windows, Rain Shadow reaches 50 mm in only 44.0% and 58.6% of cell-years, proving lack of organized multi-day wetting events.

validation_variables_classification.methodological_critique: Phase 7 variables provided robust empirical support for regime differentiation, but Category A and B metrics shared substantial mutual information with clustering inputs. The truly independent agricultural validation rests on Category C metrics (delayed sowing frequency and post-trigger break risk).

institutional_evidence.institution: ICAR-CRIDA (Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture, Hyderabad)
institutional_evidence.publication_title: Agricultural Contingency Plan for District: Solapur (State: Maharashtra)
institutional_evidence.recommended_window: Late June to July 15 for Kharif (if delayed, transition to Rabi)
institutional_evidence.rainfall_criteria: Minimum 50-75 mm cumulative rainfall wetting top 15 cm soil layer
institutional_evidence.target_crops: Pearl Millet (Bajra ICTP-8203, Shradha), Pigeonpea (Vipula, BSMR-736), Sunflower (Phule Bhaskar)
institutional_evidence.soil_and_irrigation_context: Western Maharashtra Scarcity Zone (MH-6); shallow to medium Vertisols/Inceptisols; 85% rainfed. Highly Rabi-dependent.

institutional_evidence.institution: MPKV Rahuri (Mahatma Phule Krishi Vidyapeeth, Rahuri)
institutional_evidence.publication_title: Dryland Farming Technology & Kharif Contingency Crop Planning for Scarcity Zone
institutional_evidence.recommended_window: June 15 to July 7; strict cessation after July 15
institutional_evidence.rainfall_criteria: 75 mm Rule: Minimum 75 mm soaking monsoon rain wetting 15-20 cm root zone before sowing
institutional_evidence.target_crops: Bajra (Phule Aadishakti), Red Gram (Phule Rajeshwari), Soybean (Phule Sangam - irrigated/transition only)
institutional_evidence.soil_and_irrigation_context: Rain-Shadow Scarcity Zone; heavy cracking Vertisols; dryland rainfed farming prone to seedling desiccation.

institutional_evidence.institution: VNMKV Parbhani (Vasantrao Naik Marathwada Krishi Vidyapeeth, Parbhani)
institutional_evidence.publication_title: Kharif Crop Production Technologies & Sowing Advisories for Marathwada
institutional_evidence.rainfall_criteria: 75 mm to 100 mm cumulative monsoon rainfall to prevent re-sowing risk
institutional_evidence.target_crops: Soybean (MAUS-71, MAUS-158, MAUS-162), Cotton (Bt hybrids), Pigeonpea (BDN-711)
institutional_evidence.soil_and_irrigation_context: Deep Black Cotton Soils (Vertisols) with high water retention but high initial swelling requirement.

institutional_evidence.institution: Dr. PDKV Akola (Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Krishi Vidyapeeth, Akola)
institutional_evidence.publication_title: Package of Practices for Kharif Crops of Vidarbha Region
institutional_evidence.recommended_window: June 15 to June 30 (Normal); up to July 15 (Delayed)
institutional_evidence.rainfall_criteria: 75 mm to 100 mm cumulative rainfall before sowing in heavy soils
institutional_evidence.target_crops: Soybean (JS-335, JS-93-05, PDKV AMS-100-39), Cotton (AKH-081), Tur (PKV Tara)
institutional_evidence.soil_and_irrigation_context: Core Vidarbha Vertisols; synchronized onset allows reliable early sowing with low break risk.

phase_8_decision.justification: The four K-Means K=4 regimes demonstrate strong, statistically verified agronomic differentiation. However, a naive single-threshold 50 mm trigger cannot be used directly in farmer-facing advisories for the Rain Shadow due to severe false-triggering risk (39.1% probability of 10-day post-trigger dry spell).
mandatory_phase_8_constraints: Adopt MPKV Rahuri's '75 mm Rule' for Scarcity Zone: Rainfed sowing in Rain Shadow must require >= 75 mm cumulative rainfall.
Implement a Two-Stage Trigger Rule: Require cumulative rainfall threshold PLUS a minimum of 2 wet days within 5 days to confirm sustained monsoon activity before issuing a sowing green signal.
Provide Explicit Post-Sowing Break Warnings: Flag high desiccation risk in Rain Shadow advisories and promote contingent cropping (Bajra/Pigeonpea intercropping or transition to Rabi).
Soil-Specific Stratification: Distinguish heavy Vertisols (requiring 75-100 mm) from shallow Inceptisols in advisory recommendations.
